clue.text: Even though rejected with reprimand, unlikely to flare up

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the short word for 'even though' is read backwards

parts.note: 'if' can mean 'even though', as in 'pleasant if dull'
a reproof is a rebuke or reprimand

explanation.surface: Someone reprimanded and rebuffed nonetheless stays calm and won't lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives FI. 'Even though' reads as a sentence opener, and 'flare up' suggests temper rather than flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Material resistant to burning will not catch alight or burst into flames.

clue.text: Scrap plane journey, having no money

indicators.note: having no money means the letter standing for money is taken out of the journey word

parts.note: a journey by plane is a flight
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: A traveller can't afford the airfare and has to cancel the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes L from FLIGHT. 'Scrap' looks like a verb (cancel) but is the noun meaning a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: Athletic event broadcast to people

parts.note: to relay a programme is to broadcast it
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A sports meeting is being televised to the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A track competition in which team members run successive legs, passing a baton.

clue.text: Cutting entertainment short, firmly fix seating order

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims its final letter, here the last of the entertainment word
short, together with cutting, says the entertainment word loses its last letter

parts.note: a play is a stage entertainment
to cement something is to fix it firmly

explanation.surface: Someone abbreviates a show to settle who sits where at the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting ... short' brackets the entertainment word and trims its final letter; 'firmly fix' reads as an instruction but just supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Placement is the arrangement of guests at a formal dinner table.

clue.text: Points out cause of one's being misled like this?

definitions.text: Points out cause of one's being misled like this?

parts.words: Points out cause of one's being misled like this?
parts.note: railway points that are out of order send a train down the wrong line, which is also an idiom for someone mistaken

explanation.surface: Someone identifies why a person was misled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points out' reads as 'indicates'; it means faulty railway points, which would divert a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being mistaken or pursuing a mistaken line of thought, literally a train on a wrong line.

clue.text: Full of ideas over residential development in cradle of civilisation

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another means it comes first

parts.note: a fertile mind is full of ideas
a crescent is a curved street of houses

explanation.surface: An imaginative planner oversees a housing estate in an ancient region.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain many residential streets are named Crescent, a curved terrace of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of fertile land from Mesopotamia to the Nile, where early agriculture and cities arose.

clue.text: Allow out of bed to relax

parts.note: to let is to allow
someone up is out of bed

explanation.surface: Letting someone get up out of bed so they can unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off or slacken effort, a phrasal verb for reducing intensity.

clue.text: Philosopher making secure point

parts.note: to lock is to make secure
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone fastening a door while making an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: Time needed to overcome breach in church council here

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming another piece means sitting above it, so this letter comes first

parts.note: a rent is a tear or breach

explanation.surface: A church council takes time to heal a schism.
explanation.walkthrough: The Council of Trent (1545-63) met at Trento in Italy; 'here' points to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Counter-Reformation council took its name from the Italian city where it convened.

clue.text: Law groups made haste without pressure, and missed only one point of law?

definitions.text: missed only one point of law?

parts.note: posses are groups gathered by a sheriff to enforce the law

indicators.note: without pressure means the letter for pressure is dropped from the haste word

parts.note: sped means hurried
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Lawmen hurry on and come within a whisker of the legal point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes P from SPED. The definition plays on the saying that possession is nine points of the law: owning gives you all but one.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something gives nine of the law's ten points, per the proverb, so an owner lacks just one.

clue.text: Brave young lady left a testament

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl or young woman
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A courageous girl leaves a will behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes someone courageous and chivalrous in action.

clue.text: Rows for sport

definitions.meaning: a court game played with bats and a hard ball

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: din or uproar, and a fast indoor ball game.

clue.text: Your old baffling disease is simple

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
ME (myalgic encephalomyelitis) is a poorly understood illness

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned diagnosis that is supposedly uncomplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a medicinal herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old term for a plant used as medicine; this herb is one.

clue.text: Erect pine crashes where disaster's most severe

indicators.note: crashes suggests things smashed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tall pine tree falls at the heart of a disaster zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above an earthquake's focus, where the damage is greatest.

clue.text: Sacred text worked into tiny fabric pattern

indicators.note: one piece is worked into another, set inside it

parts.note: wee means tiny
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A verse of scripture is embroidered into a small cloth design.
explanation.definitionFit: A weave is the way threads are interlaced, giving a textile its pattern.

clue.text: Knowing excellent joke

parts.note: wise means knowing
crack means first-rate, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: A shrewd, first-class quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, flippant remark made to amuse.

clue.text: Takes back fruit, first of several goods to be moved out

indicators.note: the fruit word holds several G letters and only the first of them goes
moved out means taken away from the fruit word

parts.note: greengages are green plums
G is short for good, so goods are G's

explanation.surface: A shopper returns produce after the first items are cleared from stock.
explanation.walkthrough: GREENGAGES has three Gs; 'first of several' and 'to be moved out' drop only the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-engage is to hire or employ again, taking someone back on.

clue.text: One needs energy to maul furiously hard in crucial area of field

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild, frantic movement, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A rugby forward needs vigour to tackle fiercely near the try line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' makes ALMOUT. The rugby maul is surface colour; 'One needs' is only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The area in front of the goal in football, where scoring chances are decided.

clue.text: Material son's written in drink leading to downfall

indicators.note: written in means set inside another word

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or drink generally
S is the abbreviation for son
rain is a downfall from the sky

explanation.surface: A son's drinking leads to his ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' gives GROSG. 'downfall' looks like ruin after drinking but means rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed silk or rayon fabric used for ribbons.

clue.text: Cane, say, for bribe

definitions.meaning: cane sugar is an example of something that sweetens
a bribe is a payment to make someone more agreeable

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something adding sugariness to food, and an inducement to win someone over.

clue.text: Permitted to speak in normal voice

indicators.note: to speak means the word is said rather than written, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: permitted means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone given permission to talk at an ordinary volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking audibly rather than silently or in a whisper.

clue.text: Old writer that's made a knight never mixes with cast

definitions.text: Old writer that's made a knight

indicators.note: mixes with says these letters are blended together and rearranged

explanation.surface: An author knighted for his work refuses to mix with actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a knight' sounds like being knighted, but the writer created one: Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes, the Spanish novelist, created the deluded knight Don Quixote.

clue.text: Check root that's come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tuber is a swollen underground root

explanation.surface: Inspecting a root vegetable that has sprouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's come up' turns TUBER over, reading upward in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute or repel, to check an argument or attack.

clue.text: Anger with refusal, in any case

indicators.note: in, with case, places the refusal inside the other word
case suggests a container, so the word for any wraps round the refusal

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Being refused makes people angry whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in any case' reads as the idiom 'anyway'; here 'in' and 'case' make the any word a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy is to irritate or anger someone.

clue.text: Soldier wearing protective gear for possibly dangerous spells

indicators.note: one who wears clothes is inside them, so the soldier goes within the gear

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) protects against rain
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in protective clothing faces hazardous periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spells' looks like periods of time; here it means incantations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery consists of charms and incantations, which can be harmful.

clue.text: Set free, but bound over?

definitions.meaning: to set free is to release or acquit someone
to leap over a hurdle without touching it; legally bound over is the opposite of being let off

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to release and to vault over an obstacle cleanly.

clue.text: State employing veto, inter alia

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between, so the veto goes between the letters of alia

parts.note: a ban is a veto

explanation.surface: A nation imposes a veto among other measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' is a Latin phrase meaning 'among other things'; split, 'inter' (between) becomes a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a country in the Balkans, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: European project has recent rival

parts.note: EMU, European Monetary Union, is a Europe-wide project
late means recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: A new competitor appears in a European scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rival' looks like a noun but is the verb, to equal.
explanation.definitionFit: To try to match or equal another, to strive to compete with them.

clue.text: Pet fed with chips?

definitions.meaning: a pet name for a cat
in card games, the pool is fed by players' gambling chips

explanation.definitionFit: Both a cat and a pot of shared money or stakes in a game.

clue.text: Old soldier given encouragement to include name on equipment

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: to include means to contain, so the name letter goes inside

parts.note: cheer is encouragement

explanation.surface: A veteran is cheered when his name is put on his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' gives CHENER, and 'on' puts it after the equipment. Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Kitchener was a British field marshal famous from First World War recruiting posters.
